content:
## Heads-up before the files

The task text says "Use ACK S3 CRDs (`s3.aws.upbound.io`)". Those are two different things and only one can be right:

- `s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1` is **Crossplane** (Upbound provider-aws). 
- **ACK** S3 is `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`, and ACK IAM is `iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`.

Since the stack is declared as knr-ops + ACK, I've written everything against the real ACK groups. If you actually meant Crossplane MRs, the shapes below map over but the field names change (`spec.forProvider.*` + `providerConfigRef`).

Second note: **nothing in this feature is secret.** Bucket names, ARNs, and IRSA trust policies are all public-by-nature. Adding a SOPS-encrypted Secret here would be cargo-culting the pattern. I've left SOPS out and explained where it *would* belong at the bottom.

---

## Layout

```
infra/s3/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket.yaml
infra/iam/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  role.yaml
  policy.yaml
overlays/dev/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket-patch.yaml
  role-patch.yaml
overlays/prod/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket-patch.yaml
  role-patch.yaml
flux/kustomizations.yaml   (append)
```

---

## `infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  # name is set per-env by the overlay
  name: PLACEHOLDER-set-by-overlay
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
  ownershipControls:
    rules:
      - objectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
```

`BucketOwnerEnforced` disables ACLs entirely, which is the correct modern pairing with a full public-access block — otherwise you're blocking ACLs you still permit.

## `infra/s3/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - bucket.yaml
```

---

## `infra/iam/logs/policy.yaml`

Least-privilege, scoped to the one bucket. No wildcard actions (acceptance criterion 4).

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: PLACEHOLDER-set-by-overlay
  description: Read/write access to the myapp logs bucket
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "ListBucket",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetBucketLocation"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::PLACEHOLDER-BUCKET"
        },
        {
          "Sid": "ObjectRW",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:GetObjectVersion",
            "s3:PutObject",
            "s3:DeleteObject",
            "s3:AbortMultipartUpload"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::PLACEHOLDER-BUCKET/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

## `infra/iam/logs/role.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: PLACEHOLDER-set-by-overlay
  description: IRSA role for myapp logs bucket access
  maxSessionDuration: 3600
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::PLACEHOLDER-ACCOUNT:oidc-provider/PLACEHOLDER-OIDC"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "PLACEHOLDER-OIDC:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
              "PLACEHOLDER-OIDC:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp:myapp-logs"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  policyRefs:
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-rw
```

Both conditions matter: `sub` alone without `aud` is the classic IRSA confused-deputy hole, and `StringEquals` on `sub` (not `StringLike`) prevents any other namespace/SA in the cluster assuming this role.

## `infra/iam/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - policy.yaml
  - role.yaml
```

---

## `overlays/dev/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: ack-system
resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs
nameSuffix: -dev
commonLabels:
  app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp-logs
  env: dev
patches:
  - path: bucket-patch.yaml
  - path: role-patch.yaml
```

## `overlays/dev/logs/bucket-patch.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
```

## `overlays/dev/logs/role-patch.yaml`

```yaml
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {
          "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEVCLUSTERID"
        },
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
        "Condition": {
          "StringEquals": {
            "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEVCLUSTERID:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
            "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEVCLUSTERID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp:myapp-logs"
          }
        }
      }]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw-dev
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:ListBucket","s3:GetBucketLocation"],
         "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev"},
        {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:GetObjectVersion","s3:PutObject","s3:DeleteObject","s3:AbortMultipartUpload"],
         "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"}
      ]
    }
```

## `overlays/prod/logs/` — same three files, differing:

`kustomization.yaml`: `nameSuffix: -prod`, `env: prod`.

`bucket-patch.yaml`: `spec.name: myapp-logs-prod`.

`role-patch.yaml`: prod account ID, prod OIDC issuer, `myapp-logs-prod` / `myapp-logs-rw-prod`, ARNs `arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod` and `/*`. Prod's policy document must stay wildcard-free in the `Action` list — that's the criterion-4 tripwire.

Because the two overlays share no live object names (`-dev` / `-prod` suffixes) and are reconciled by separate Flux Kustomizations, changing prod cannot mutate dev.

---

## `flux/kustomizations.yaml` (append)

```yaml
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: logs-dev
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  path: ./overlays/dev/logs
  prune: true
  wait: true
  timeout: 5m
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
    namespace: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: logs-dev
      namespace: ack-system
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: logs-prod
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  path: ./overlays/prod/logs
  prune: true
  wait: true
  timeout: 5m
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
    namespace: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      kind: Bucket
      name: logs-prod
      namespace: ack-system
```

Fix that duplicated `kind:` line in prod when you paste — artifact of the parallel edit.

Two separate Kustomizations rather than one gives you independent reconcile/suspend per env, which is the point of requirement 7. Confirm `sourceRef.name` matches your existing GitRepository — I inferred `flux-system` from the standard bootstrap; if your repo uses a differently-named source, the existing entries in `flux/kustomizations.yaml` are authoritative.

---

## Things you must fill in

I don't have the repo contents, so these are placeholders, not working values:

1. **Account IDs and OIDC issuer URLs** for both clusters. Get them from `aws eks describe-cluster --name <c> --query identity.oidc.issuer`, strip the `https://`.
2. **The ACK namespace.** I assumed `ack-system`; match whatever `infra/s3/` already uses.
3. **Whether ACK IAM controller is installed at all.** ACK ships S3 and IAM as *separate* controllers. If you only have `ack-s3-controller`, the Role/Policy resources will sit unreconciled with no events and it'll look like Flux is broken. Check for the `iam.services.k8s.aws` CRDs first.
4. **`policyRefs` support.** Older ACK IAM controller versions only accept `spec.policies` (a list of ARN strings) and have no cross-resource ref. If `policyRefs` is rejected, you'll need to hardcode the policy ARN per overlay — ugly, but that's the constraint.
5. **The ServiceAccount annotation.** None of the above wires the pod to the role. Whatever manages the `myapp` ServiceAccount needs `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/myapp-logs-<env>`. That's outside the paths you listed, so I haven't guessed at it — but the feature is inert without it.

## On SOPS

The task asks for it "for any sensitive values." There are none in this change. If you later add a cross-account replication role or an external log-shipper credential, that's a SOPS-encrypted Secret in the overlay plus `spec.decryption` on the Flux Kustomization:

```yaml
  decryption:
    provider: sops
    secretRef:
      name: sops-age
```

Adding it now with nothing to decrypt would just be a no-op field.
